solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit consignment one copper leaves for actor

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so that element is dropped from the front of the build

blocks.note: botanically a cucumber is a fruit
a batch is a lot sent or made together
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A shipment of fruit arrives and a policeman walks off in favour of an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: CUCUMBER BATCH loses its opening CU to leave CUMBERBATCH; 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedict Cumberbatch is a famous English stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Leave fair with Dicky

blocks.note: fair weather is clear weather
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as is off

explanation.surface: Someone told to depart a funfair along with a friend called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; in British slang it means poorly or unsound.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off is an informal imperative or verb for going away, departing.

clue.text: Activist set on fire by American in plant

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the plant, so the plant word wraps around them

blocks.note: mint is a herb
lit means ignited
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A protester torches an American factory, or so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant is a combative campaigner, a synonym for an aggressive activist.

clue.text: Mentioned college as courses enjoyed?

definitions.note: read as 'courses (that have been) enjoyed', a past participle

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the college name counts by its sound

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school, pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A remark about a school's dinners, wondering whether the meals went down well.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boarding school; said aloud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses of a meal that have been consumed with pleasure are ones that were swallowed, past participle of eat.

clue.text: Suet bit suspect in sandwiches

indicators.note: a suspect thing is not to be trusted as given, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of a lump of suet found in their lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is a northern English word for a sandwich, as in chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: Butties is informal British slang for filled bread rolls or slices: plural sandwiches.

clue.text: Paddy ace in painting technique

blocks.note: in British slang a paddy is a fit of temper
A stands for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy is brilliant at a particular style of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name; in British usage it is a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a method of painting with pigment bound in egg yolk.

clue.text: Past master broadcast this on air

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert tells a presenter to put something on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past master' normally means an expert; here it is read literally as a master of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies earlier times is, read literally, an authority on bygone events.

clue.text: Glaswegian perhaps lacking Charlie in boozer

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is taken out

blocks.note: someone from Glasgow is an example of a Scot
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A Glasgow drinker in the pub, missing his pal Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT without its C leaves the answer; 'boozer' is also British slang for a pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a habitual drunkard, a synonym for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Man on a 13 18 location

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: to man a post is to staff it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to crew a site in the Hebrides, referring to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 18 is FINGAL'S CAVE, the sea cave on the Hebridean island of Staffa off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is the uninhabited Scottish island where Fingal's Cave is found.

clue.text: See 28
Chapter in story reversed brilliant success

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the story word from back to front
the chapter abbreviation is placed within the story word

blocks.note: a tale is a story
C is the usual abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A novel in which one chapter turned events round, making it a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat, borrowed from French, means a dazzling display of achievement or acclaim.

clue.text: Intoxicant consumed in restraint for duration

indicators.note: something consumed in another is swallowed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tie is a binding or restriction
mescal is a hallucinogen from cactus, also a spirit

explanation.surface: A drug taken under restraint over a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the length of time over which something happens, its span.

clue.text: Such memories good about wine Neo has

definitions.note: a phrase read as 'what memories that are good are'

blocks.note: re means concerning
tent is a deep-red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite
Neo is the setter, so 'Neo has' is I've

explanation.surface: The setter reminisces about wine he has enjoyed, with fond memories.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym; Neo has becomes I've.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory is one that holds on to information well, i.e. a good one.

clue.text: Tender assassin?

blocks.note: first meaning: to put forward a proposal or bid
second meaning, whimsical: one who 'offs' someone, slang for kills

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender assassin' reads as a gentle killer; the question mark flags the invented second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer is to tender a bid; and someone who offs people, slang for killing, is jokingly an offer.

clue.text: Student into saving face mismanaged overture

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the student's letter joins the other letters
something mismanaged is badly organised, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is a learner driver's plate, crossword shorthand for student
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student's attempt to avoid embarrassment over a botched advance goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overture' looks like a peace approach; it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's Hebrides Overture is also known by the name of the Scottish sea cave that inspired it.

clue.text: A better jazz singer without piano, unaccompanied

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the piano letter is surrounded

blocks.note: taken as written
to cap is to outdo
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Ella Fitzgerald, the great jazz vocalist

explanation.surface: A superior jazz vocalist performing with no pianist, singing alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'on the outside of', so the piano is surrounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed with voices alone, without instrumental backing.

clue.text: Greedy old king sacrificing first daughter

indicators.note: giving up the opening letter, so the front of the name is lost

blocks.note: David, the Biblical king of Israel
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A grasping ancient monarch gives up his eldest daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, sometimes to the point of being grasping.

clue.text: What might get me in post corruptly?

definitions.text: What might get me in post corruptly?

indicators.note: corruptly suggests something twisted out of true, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how they might wangle a job through dishonest means.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while the letters of 'me in post' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism to relatives in appointments, a way to land a job unfairly.

clue.text: Lowbrow loony means to pen classical number

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the following letters go haywire
to pen is to enclose, so one piece is shut inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
sex is Latin for six

explanation.surface: A crude madman uses some device to write classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex Man is a British stereotype of a brash, materialistic voter from the county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex Man is a derogatory caricature of an uncultured, vulgar working-class figure.

clue.text: See 13
Discomfort each Biblical wife reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the name loses its last letter

blocks.note: ea is the abbreviation for each
Rachel was Jacob's wife

explanation.surface: Each of the Bible's wives suffers a lessening of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is a pain in the ear, a specific kind of bodily discomfort.

clue.text: Certain things from Thames & Hudson perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: in betting, sure-fire selections
second meaning: crossword whimsy for rivers, things that have banks

explanation.walkthrough: Thames & Hudson is a real publishing house, which misleads; here the Thames and the Hudson are rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankers are sure bets in pools or racing; rivers, which have banks, are punningly called bankers.

clue.text: See 28
Fish tails in sausage meat for hound

indicators.note: tails are the end parts, so only the final letters are kept

blocks.note: a bass is a fish
the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Fish ends up in sausage meat fed to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Pen one used during this writer's block

indicators.note: something used during another sits in the middle of it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a sty is a pig pen
the setter referring to himself
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A writer's block, with one pen in use the whole time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' looks like a phrase; the definition is just 'block'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart someone's plans.

clue.text: Behave badly in a court before a judge

blocks.note: taken as written
ct is an abbreviation for court
to be up before the magistrate is to appear in the dock

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves in a courtroom while facing the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, especially to play up like a naughty child.

clue.text: Palaver bringing motorway through capital part

indicators.note: something going through another runs inside it

blocks.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
M denotes a British motorway, as in M1
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A fuss about building a major road through part of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious procedure, the same as a palaver or fuss.

clue.text: Medical Officer succeeding after mission

indicators.note: succeeding means following on, so the officer comes second

blocks.note: à la means in the manner of, after
MO is the abbreviation for Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A doctor takes over after a mission abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission, famous for the 1836 siege.

clue.text: Images from eccentric musical artist

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are shifted about

blocks.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Pictures produced by an oddball musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are likenesses or representations, plural of simulacrum.

clue.text: Saw US chopper land in Irish Sea

blocks.note: ax is the American spelling of axe
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an American helicopter landing in the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, and 'chopper' like a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, and an axiom is an accepted principle or maxim.

clue.text: Critical report in articles appearing with Circle Line series

indicators.note: in places one piece between the two articles

blocks.note: two instances of the definite article
critical as in big, important; a report is a bang
a circle is O-shaped
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A newspaper review of a London Underground route sounds like a negative report.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle Line looks like the London Underground line, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang Theory is the long-running American TV sitcom, a television series.

clue.text: Some spirit — grotesque demon in film

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted, so the letters are twisted into a new shape

blocks.note: a few means some
go is energy or verve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie featuring some sort of ghastly demonic spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Few Good Men is a 1992 courtroom drama movie starring Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson.
